- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often over-anticipates spikes; reduce forecast peak values and smooth downward corrections.
- Model frequently over-estimates short-term spikes (especially 1-3 day horizons) after sentiment shifts; apply dampening factor to spikes >2x historical mean.
- Model under-estimates long-term (15+ day) trends when sentiment is stable; adjust forecast upward by 10-20% if sentiment remains flat or mildly positive.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.33/1.00 alternation, model exhibits oscillatory bias; apply smoothing filter to reduce amplitude of forecast swings.
- Model consistently under-forecasts true values in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; add 0.1–0.3 to forecast if sentiment <0.5 over last 5 days.
- Avoid forecasting >3x historical max in 30-day horizon unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) and recent price is rising; cap at 2x historical max for safety.
